_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Forms roadmap rendered at /docs/extensions/forms/roadmap. Task `status` is maintained AUTOMATICALLY by `npm run roadmap:forms` (scripts/gen-roadmap.mjs), which inspects the real extension source tree and flips a task to `done` when everything in its `detect` block exists. The detect paths are the extension's agreed file layout: core classes in includes/<area>/, each field type in includes/option-types/form-builder/items/<type>/, each on-submit step in includes/actions/, the element in extensions/contact-forms/shortcodes/contact-form/. Hand-edit title/detail/detect freely; set `pin: true` on a task whose status the script should leave alone.

milestones.title: Phase 0 · What Forms already does
milestones.goal: The base every later phase builds on: a drag-and-drop form builder inside the Contact Form element, stored entries, conditional fields, on-submit actions other extensions add to, and ready-made starter forms.

tasks.title: Stored entries
tasks.detail: Every submission is kept under Unyson+ → Form Entries, even when the notification email fails: search, status views, date filter, bulk archive or delete, CSV export, a retention period, and the WordPress personal-data export and erase tools.

tasks.title: Field types
tasks.detail: Text, textarea, email, website, number, select, radio, checkboxes, date and time, star or score rating, hidden values, consent boxes and private file uploads.

tasks.title: Conditional fields
tasks.detail: Any field can be shown only when another field has a given answer. The rule is also enforced on the server, so a hidden field is never checked or collected.

tasks.title: On-submit actions
tasks.detail: A per-form list of steps that run after a submission. Forms ships Store entry; the CRM adds Add to the CRM and Membership adds Register member. Any extension can register its own.

tasks.title: Starter forms
tasks.detail: Nine ready-made forms in the builder's Templates panel: Contact, Appointment request, Table booking, Quote request, Event registration, Support ticket, Feedback, NPS survey and Newsletter signup.

tasks.title: Spam protection
tasks.detail: A hidden honeypot field, Google reCAPTCHA, and a limit on how many forms one visitor can send in ten minutes.

tasks.title: AI Assistant abilities
tasks.detail: A connected AI can describe the field types and starters and place a form with its actions. It never sees the entries.

milestones.title: Phase 1 · Form Styles presets
milestones.goal: Field styling moves onto presets in Theme Settings, the same rule buttons and boxes already follow, so every form on a site matches and one edit restyles them all. The Contact Form element picks a style; its own Style tab keeps only what belongs to that one form.

tasks.title: Form Styles presets in Theme Settings
tasks.detail: Theme Settings → Components → Form Styles: field background, text, border, focus colour and ring, placeholder, label, help, error and choice colours; border width, box or underline, corner radius, height, side padding and text size; label size, weight and case; separate colours for site dark mode; and custom CSS. Ships Standard, Soft, Underline, Rounded and On Dark (for forms on dark sections).

tasks.title: Form style picker on the element
tasks.detail: The Contact Form element's Style tab has a Form Style dropdown. Its own field settings remain as "this form only" overrides that win over the preset; width, alignment and spacing stay per form. The submit button keeps using the Button presets.

tasks.title: Existing forms keep their look
tasks.detail: Standard reproduces the original field look exactly and is the default, so existing forms render the same. A form whose style was renamed or deleted falls back to plain fields.

tasks.title: One style for every form on the site
tasks.detail: The same Form Styles reach the Newsletter element and Membership's forms, and the Site Converter maps a source site's input styling into a preset.

milestones.title: Phase 2 · Better sending: accessible, instant and trusted
milestones.goal: The basics every form on every site benefits from, before any new form type: sending without a page reload, errors everyone can find and fix, the sender getting a copy, and stronger spam protection.

tasks.title: Send without reloading the page
tasks.detail: The form sends in the background and shows its message in place; the page no longer reloads and jumps back to the top. Forms still work with JavaScript off, falling back to today's reload.

tasks.title: Accessible error messages
tasks.detail: Each problem is described in words next to its field and linked to it for screen readers (aria-invalid and aria-describedby); a long form gets a summary at the top; focus moves to the first problem; colour is never the only signal. Follows WCAG 2.2 success criteria 3.3.1, 3.3.3 and 1.4.1.

tasks.title: Autofill hints
tasks.detail: Name, email, phone and address fields declare what they hold, so browsers and password managers fill them in and assistive tools can recognise them (WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.3.5).

tasks.title: What happens after sending
tasks.detail: Keep the form and show the message, replace the form with the message, go to a thank-you page, or go to any address, with answers usable in the message and the address.

tasks.title: A confirmation email to the sender
tasks.detail: An on-submit action that emails the person who sent the form a copy of their answers or a custom message, with the site's email styling.

tasks.title: CC, BCC and answer tags in notifications
tasks.detail: CC and BCC on the notification email, the admin email when no recipient is set, and answer tags such as {text_name} or {all_fields} in the subject and the messages.

tasks.title: Cloudflare Turnstile and hCaptcha
tasks.detail: Two more spam checks beside reCAPTCHA. Turnstile is free with no usage cap and usually shows nothing to real visitors.

tasks.title: Content spam filtering
tasks.detail: Check submissions against Akismet when it is installed, and against a site list of blocked words, email domains and a link limit. A caught submission still sees the normal success message, sends nothing and is kept as Spam in Entries rather than lost.

tasks.title: Several notifications, routed by answer
tasks.detail: More than one notification per form, recipients chosen by an answer (sales questions to sales, support to support), and a different after-sending outcome depending on the answers.

milestones.title: Phase 3 · Choose a form type first
milestones.goal: The starter forms stop being hidden in the builder's Templates panel. Adding a Contact Form element opens a picker of form types first, then the same builder as today.

tasks.title: Starter picker on a new form
tasks.detail: A new Contact Form element opens with the form types, grouped, each with a short description and its number of fields, plus Blank. Picking one fills the builder and the subject, button and thank-you text; everything stays editable. "Choose a form type" in the builder header reopens it. (Saved forms join the picker with the form library.)

tasks.title: More starter types
tasks.detail: Callback request, product enquiry, RSVP, job application, volunteer sign-up and a download (lead magnet), on top of the nine starters. A quiz starter follows quiz scoring.

tasks.title: Describe a form, get a form
tasks.detail: In the picker, describe the form in a sentence and the site's AI provider (connected through WordPress's AI Client) builds the fields and texts for you to edit. Every field is checked before it reaches the builder.

milestones.title: Phase 4 · The form library
milestones.goal: Forms become things you build once and place anywhere, the model Gravity Forms and WPForms use. Unyson+ → Forms lists every form; the Contact Form element shows one of them.

tasks.title: Saved forms
tasks.detail: A form is stored once (a private post type), with its fields, settings and actions, and keeps a stable id, so entries group by real form instead of by page.

tasks.title: Forms screen
tasks.detail: Unyson+ → Forms, beside Form Entries: every form with its number of fields, its entries and the pages it is placed on. Add New starts from the form-type picker; Duplicate, Export and Import a form as JSON.

tasks.title: The element picks a saved form
tasks.detail: The Contact Form element chooses a saved form (Form Fields → Saved Form), so editing it once updates every page that shows it; the element keeps its own Style. A form built inside an element keeps working and has a "Save to the library" link; saved forms also appear in the picker.

tasks.title: Form history and undo
tasks.detail: Every save of a form is kept as a WordPress revision, so an earlier version can be compared and restored.

milestones.title: Phase 5 · Longer forms and richer fields
milestones.goal: What application, registration and intake forms need: steps, and fields that collect a person's details properly.

tasks.title: Multi-step forms
tasks.detail: A Page Break field splits a form into steps with a progress bar, Back and Next. Each step is checked before moving on, an error found on sending opens the step it belongs to, and without JavaScript the whole form shows at once with each break as a heading.

tasks.title: Name field
tasks.detail: Full name in one box, or first and last name side by side, with the right autofill on each.

tasks.title: Phone field
tasks.detail: A phone box that brings up the number keypad, accepts the usual international formats and fills in from the browser.

tasks.title: Address field
tasks.detail: Street, an optional second line, city, an optional region, postcode and country, each with its own autofill; the country can be filled in for the visitor.

tasks.title: Section headings and text
tasks.detail: A heading-and-text block to explain a part of the form between fields. It collects nothing.

tasks.title: Repeating groups
tasks.detail: A set of fields a visitor can add again ("add another guest", "add another job"), each copy stored as its own row.

tasks.title: Picture choices, ranking, sliders and grids
tasks.detail: Choices shown as image cards, a ranking with Move up / Move down buttons (or dropdowns without JavaScript), a range slider showing its value, and a survey grid (several statements on one scale) that stacks on phones.

tasks.title: Pre-filled and piped answers
tasks.detail: Fill fields from the address, the logged-in user or the CRM contact, and repeat an earlier answer later in the form ("Thanks, {name}. Which date suits you?").

tasks.title: One question at a time
tasks.detail: An optional layout that shows one question per screen, with keyboard navigation and a progress bar. The same form can be shown either way.

tasks.title: Floating labels
tasks.detail: A Form Styles option that places the label inside the field and moves it above while typing, without losing the label for screen readers.

milestones.title: Phase 6 · Calculations and payments
milestones.goal: Forms that work out a price and take the money: quotes, simple orders, deposits and donations, without a shop.

tasks.title: Calculated field
tasks.detail: A total worked out from other answers (quantity × price, options that add to a base price), shown live and recalculated on the server.

tasks.title: Product and amount fields
tasks.detail: A product with a price and quantity, and a pay-what-you-want amount for donations, with suggested amounts.

tasks.title: Take payment action
tasks.detail: An on-submit action that charges the form's total by card through Stripe or through PayPal. The entry records the payment and its status; a failed payment keeps the entry and tells the visitor.

tasks.title: Coupons
tasks.detail: Fixed or percentage discount codes on payment forms, with limits on uses and dates.

tasks.title: Recurring payments
tasks.detail: Monthly or yearly charges for donations and simple subscriptions, cancellable by the payer.

tasks.title: Pay later
tasks.detail: A bank transfer or pay-on-arrival choice that records the amount owed and is marked paid by hand.

milestones.title: Phase 7 · Quizzes, limits and more
milestones.goal: The remaining form types from the common list, and the tools long or popular forms need.

tasks.title: Quiz scoring
tasks.detail: Points per answer, a total score, and a different message, redirect or CRM tag for each score range. Covers knowledge quizzes and product-finder quizzes.

tasks.title: Entry and seat limits
tasks.detail: Close a form after a number of entries, on a date, or once each choice's seats are taken ("Saturday workshop: 3 places left"), with a message shown when it is full.

tasks.title: Save and continue later
tasks.detail: A visitor can save a long form part-way and get a link by email to finish it.

tasks.title: Signature field
tasks.detail: Draw a signature with a mouse or finger, stored privately with the entry like a file upload.

tasks.title: Create a post action
tasks.detail: Turn a submission into a draft post or a custom post type entry (a listing, a testimonial, an event), with fields mapped to the title, content, featured image and custom fields.

tasks.title: Survey results
tasks.detail: A results view per form: answer counts and charts for choice and rating fields, average scores, NPS, and the trend over time.

tasks.title: Send to a webhook action
tasks.detail: Post a submission's answers as JSON to any URL, for automation tools and other systems.

tasks.title: PDF copies of entries
tasks.detail: Turn an entry into a PDF (a receipt, an application, a signed waiver), attach it to the emails or download it from Entries.

tasks.title: Send to a spreadsheet action
tasks.detail: Add each submission as a row in a Google Sheets spreadsheet.

milestones.title: Phase 8 · See how forms perform and follow up
milestones.goal: Which forms are seen, started, finished and abandoned, and the tools to act on what comes in.

tasks.title: Form analytics
tasks.detail: Views, starts, completions and the field where people give up, per form and over time. Shares the Visitor Insights data when that extension is on.

tasks.title: Unfinished entries
tasks.detail: Optionally keep what a visitor typed into a form they did not send, so a half-finished quote request can be followed up. Off by default, and stated in the form's privacy notice when on.

tasks.title: Working with entries
tasks.detail: Notes on an entry, assign it to a team member, star it, reply from the entry, and correct an answer with the change logged.

tasks.title: Scheduled export and clean-up
tasks.detail: Email a CSV of new entries every day or week, and set retention per form instead of one site-wide period.

milestones.title: Phase 9 · Show entries on the site
milestones.goal: Use what people send as content: directories, listings and testimonials, with an approval step before anything goes public.

tasks.title: Entry views
tasks.detail: An element that shows a form's entries as a table, grid, list, map or calendar, with search, filters and a page per entry. Only the fields chosen for it are shown.

tasks.title: Approval before publishing
tasks.detail: Entries shown in a view wait for approval; an approver gets an email and can approve or reject from it.

tasks.title: People edit their own entries
tasks.detail: A logged-in person can update what they sent (a listing, an application) until it is locked.

milestones.title: Phase 10 · Bookings plug in
milestones.goal: Reservations stay a separate Bookings extension (availability, nightly or slot pricing, calendar sync). It connects to Forms the way the CRM and Membership do: by adding a field and an action, never by moving booking code into Forms.

tasks.title: Dates and availability field
tasks.detail: Supplied by the Bookings extension: a calendar that greys out taken dates or slots and shows the live price, usable in any form. First built in a rental site's own booking plugin (a "Stay dates" field checked on the server for free nights, minimum stay and guest limit); it moves into Bookings when that extension is built.

tasks.title: Reserve action
tasks.detail: Supplied by the Bookings extension: holds the chosen dates when the form is sent and re-checks that they are still free. A booking form is then a normal form with its own extra questions. First built in a rental site's own booking plugin ("Reserve the dates": creates the pending booking with the reference the thank-you message shows, and sends the owner's confirm / decline alert); Forms gained a switch to turn its own notification email off for it.
